articleTitle: Integrated Optical Phased Arrays: LiDAR, AR Displays, Biophotonics, and Beyond
abstract: Integrated optical phased arrays (OPAs), fabricated in advanced silicon-photonics platforms, enable manipulation and dynamic control of free-space light in a compact form factor, at low costs, and in a non-mechanical way. In this talk, I will highlight our work on developing OPA-based platforms, devices, and systems that enable chip-based solutions to high-impact problems in areas including augmented-reality displays, LiDAR sensing for autonomous vehicles, optical trapping for biophotonics, 3D printing, and trapped-ion quantum engineering.

articleTitle: Terahertz Blood Glucose Biosensor Using Split Ring Resonator Plasmonic Metasurface
abstract: Early detection and monitoring of diabetes ensures sound health of humans. With the recent progress in metamaterial-based sensing mechanisms, efforts have been made to introduce flat optical glucose biosensors for diabetes detection. In this paper, a plasmonic blood glucose biosensor has been proposed and analyzed with respect to changing optical parameters of blood due to changing glucose levels. The sensor operates in the terahertz regime.

articleTitle: Perovskite nanoparticles on demand: highly stable nanoparticles using reverse micelle templating
abstract: Using reverse micelle templating as a universal method for perovskites, we have been able to produce emitting particles across the visible spectrum. Both polymer and inorganic shells around the perovskite core have shown increased stability, as well as unusual room temperature crystal structures and optical properties. The slowed down reaction kinetics allows precise tuning of the compositions, sizes and distributions.

articleTitle: Automated texture-based segmentation of hair follicles in volumetric optical coherence tomography images of dermatologic burn wounds
abstract: Adnexal structures in skin, such as sweat glands and hair follicles, harbor stem cells that are indispensable for wound healing following acute injuries such as burns of various degrees [1]. Developing a method to identify and visualize these structures in the dermal layer of tissue would greatly supplement imaging studies probing burn injury depth-extent, to assess whether intact adnexal structures will contribute to wound healing and provide invaluable prognostic information in the clinic. Two methods were recently attempted for this purpose in literature but held limitations of resolution and lack of proper filtering [2, 3], thus here we present an automated segmentation algorithm for volumetrically delineating such adnexal structures as hair follicles from surrounding skin tissue by performing texture-based analysis of optical coherence tomography (OCT) images of burn wounds. OCT, a label-free imaging modality, has been previously used for burn wound examination and is ideally suited for dermatological studies demanding high resolution, real-time, and noncontact evaluation to avoid infliction of further injury and patient discomfort [4]. The proposed method is based on Gamma distribution fits of OCT speckle pattern histograms [5], with demonstrated sensitivity of the fitting parameters to follicle locations, the boundary detection of which is confirmed with histology. Our technique demonstrates high accuracy in hair follicle delineation and strong applicability to subsequent studies to assess skin regeneration potential based on follicle location in measured depth-extent of burn injury, enabling future clinical translation not only to burn wounds, but other types of skin injuries.

articleTitle: Liquid crystal assisted optical delay
abstract: Interferometry is a fundamental mechanism used to perform time-domain optical experimentation. Applications of interferometry that have implications for multiple fields of science include the autocorrelation of ultrafast lasers and terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) [1–3]. However, applications of these optical techniques can require high accuracy time-domain resolution, e.g., THz-TDS of thin films [4]. Mechanically actuated pico-motors are used to improve the resolution of coarse and large length motorized linear delay lines. However, mechanisms with moving components generally are at a disadvantage to electro-optic components because they have limitations on speed, durability, and reliability, i.e., delay stage drift [3]. In this work, a liquid crystal (LC) wave modulator is explored as a phase delay mechanism as an alternative to mechanical actuation for improvement to time-domain resolution—shown via an interferometric autocorrelation of an ultrafast pulsed laser.

articleTitle: Off-chip surface grating couplers and nano-antennas for optical communications and phased arrays
abstract: Coupling of light between integrated photonic chips and optical fibers or free-space ports requires high efficiency optical elements to accommodate demands for wide range of applications. Here, we present recent advances in the development of low-loss silicon nitride grating couplers and compact silicon-on-insulator nano-antennas with high-directionality.

articleTitle: Generation and Switching/Routing of Optical Ferris Wheel using a π-shifted Sagnac Interferometer
abstract: Optical Ferris wheel/petal beams can be generated by interference of two beams with opposite vorticity/orbital angular momentum (OAM). We present a simple scheme employing a Sagnac interferometer containing a spiral phase plate to generate such beams. A half wave plate introduced into the SI can switch the intensity pattern between the two outputs and rotate the petal beams. This can find applications in optical trapping, optical information transmission and processing/signal multiplexing/de-multiplexing when using beams with high vorticity/OAM.

articleTitle: Nonlinear optical impairments in silicon ring resonator thermometers and their mitigation
abstract: Silicon ring resonators are currently being assessed by several national metrology organizations as thermometers for use in calibration laboratories and in high-accuracy commercial applications. We show that nonlinear refractive index changes due to self-heating and free carrier generation by the interrogating light can be sources of error in temperature measurements with a Si ring-resonator thermometer. Since self-heating and carrier generation depend on material defects and the resonator structure, we show that these effects can be mitigated by optimizing the resonator design and fabrication process.

articleTitle: Phase Control in Polarization Maintaining Fiber for Quantum Key Distribution
abstract: Polarization encodings for quantum key distribution (QKD) in fiber suffer from strain- and temperature-induced polarization instabilities, which can be addressed using a polarization control system. The polarization instability can be reduced to a single phase parameter by using polarization maintaining (PM) fiber. However, phase control in PM fiber is typically applied to phase stabilization on signals coupled into only one bases of the PM fiber, making such methods insufficient for QKD which encodes signals in orthogonal bases. We describe an active system to monitor and control the phase in PM fiber to enable PM fiber based QKD systems.

articleTitle: Plasmonic photocatalysis using porous bimetallic AuPt structure
abstract: In this work, we report a facile way of fabricating a porous bimetallic alloy of AuPt sponge structure by thermal dewetting followed by a dealloying technique. The porous nature and inherent plasmonic properties of the metal components make the as-fabricated alloy an effective catalyst for driving the photodegradation of methylene blue. A considerable change is observed in the photoreduction efficiencies in presence of electron and hole scavenging species signifying the difference in the role of charge carrier.

articleTitle: High Responsivity Si/Ge Phototransistor on Silicon Photonics Platform for Small Signal Application
abstract: We report a new type of Si/Ge waveguide phototransistor with high responsivity under low bias voltages for small signal and low noise applications. The phototransistor is fabricated using a standard silicon photonics foundry and shows a responsivity higher than 500 A/W at 0.5 V bias, where the dark current is on the order of a few micron amperes.

articleTitle: Multi-Cavity Dielectric Mirrors for Spectral-Splitting Photovoltaic Applications
abstract: Dielectric optical mirrors are designed, fabricated and tested, to be used as spectral-splitting mirrors in four-terminal photovoltaic modules. Mirrors are conceived as 1D-Photonics Bandgap Materials and designed as coupled multiple Bragg reflectors. Spectral tunability, transition steepness and in-band flatness are set by tuning a whole set of parameters, namely: the number and thickness of layers for the single cavity, the number of cavities and their sequence and the adequate refractive index contrast. The final design is optimized by machine-learning. In the present case, the final structure is made of the cascade of 5 Bragg reflectors, each one formed by 4 pairs of alternated layers of SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, or SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> as a whole summing up to 41 layers. Multilayers fabrication is by Radio-Frequency sputtering deposition. Theoretical and experimental spectral curves well match. Preliminary results confirm the suitability of the fabrication technique to perform on flexible substrates, both of thin silica glass and of polyurethane resist.

articleTitle: Optical Quantum Memory In Atomic Barium With 880 GHz Bandwidth and 95% Storage Efficiency
abstract: We demonstrate quantum memory of single-photon-level coherent pulses of 880 GHz bandwidth with 95.6(3)% storage efficiency in collisionally broadened barium vapor. We measure 26(1)% total efficiency, limited by control field power; 0.49(1) ns memory lifetime, limited by motional dephasing; and a signal-to-noise ratio of ${O}(10^{3})$, limited by two-photon control field scattering. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this represents the best efficiency, lifetime, and noise performance of atomic quantum memories in the ultrabroadband regime $(\gt100$ GHz bandwidth) to date.

articleTitle: Silicon nitride subwavelength grating metamaterial waveguides functionalized with atomic layer deposited Al2O3 cladding
abstract: We report on subwavelength grating metamaterial waveguides fabricated on a rapid prototyping silicon nitride foundry platform coated in aluminum oxide grown using a post-process atomic layer deposition system. We discuss the design of the metamaterial waveguides and report experimental results for the hybrid waveguide devices.

articleTitle: ZBLAN Optical Fiber Couplers for the Mid-Infrared
abstract: A single-mode optical fiber coupler is demonstrated from ZBLAN fiber with a coupling ratio of 61%/39% at a wavelength of 2.7 $\mu$m. Single-modedness is evidenced from the absence of modal interference in the transmission spectrum. Coupling to the cross-port is limited by the onset of crystallization during the tapering process, which fosters signal loss through scattering.

articleTitle: Studying the Optical Properties of 1-Decanol for Ultrashort Pulse Generation
abstract: Motivated by our previous study of spectral broadening in 1-decanol, we further investigate its nonlinear optical properties. We observe super-continuum generation and measure a nonlinear index comparable to well-studied liquids such as carbon disulfide. To inform our calculation of the nonlinear index, we make the first reported measurement of the dispersion and index of refraction of 1-decanol. The high nonlinearity and relatively low dispersion of 1-decanol yields a simple approach to broadband pulses while maintaining phase control.

articleTitle: Simulation and Evaluation of Refractive Index-Based Sensor Platform for Bio-detection
abstract: This research focuses on evaluating the effectiveness of the gold nanoisland platform by applying the refractive index (RI) technique. The gold plasmon band’s shifts, caused by changes in the RI of the sensing medium, can provide us with valuable insights into the platform’s performance. The goal is to use this platform to detect biological molecules, making it a promising tool for future applications in this area of study.

articleTitle: Examining Confinement Loss in ANF Fibers
abstract: We design an antiresonant nodeless fiber reducing confinement loss by 9.8 dB/km in C-band and 20.4 dB/km in O-band compared to previous designs. The simpler fiber geometry may offer earlier adoption than ultra-low-loss hollow core fibers. © 2023 The Author(s)

articleTitle: Design and Study of Comb Actuated Open-Coupled Waveguide System
abstract: In recent decades, tuning the silicon photonic circuits integrated with micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS) got much attention to modify light propagation. One of the actuation types for waveguide beam steering is comb-type actuators based on the electrostatic forces. In this paper, numerical analysis of different dielectric thickness of fingers in comb-type actuator integrated with waveguide has been done. In this regard, the deflection profile of the tip of the actuator has been shown.

articleTitle: Intra-Chip Wireless Communication using RF On-Chip Antennas in Silicon Photonics
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate an intra-chip communication using RF on-chip antennas on a commercial silicon photonic platform. Two on-chip antenna topologies are presented with resonance at 15.5 GHz and 13 GHz and a maximum transmission coefficient (S21) value of -23 dB.

articleTitle: 2x2 Ultra-Broadband Multimode Interference Coupler with Subwavelength Gratings Fabricated by Immersion Lithography
abstract: We demonstrate an ultra-broadband 2x2 multimode interference (MMI) coupler leveraging subwavelength grating (SWG) nanostructures fabricated by immersion lithography. Excess loss of $\lt2$ dB, power imbalance $\lt1.5$ dB and phase error $\lt 5^{\circ}$ have been measured for a wavelength range of 1300 – 1680 nm. The small feature sizes, down to 75 nm, were well-defined using immersion lithography and optimized optical proximity correction.

articleTitle: Electro-Optic Modulator Stabilizer for Consistent Generation of Short Tunable Optical Pulses
abstract: We demonstrate a digital electro-optic modulator (EOM) bias controller designed to maximize the extinction ratio of 100ps optical pulses, which are utilized for exciting single photons from quantum dots. The optical pulses formed by this EOM, continuous-wave tunable diode laser, and electronic pulse generator are an affordable and compact alternative to pulsed Ti: Sapphire Lasers.

articleTitle: High-speed hybrid multi-mode fiber-free space optics transmission system based on orbital angular momentum multiplexed beams
abstract: The modelling of a hybrid multi-mode-fiber (MMF)-free-space-optics (FSO) transmission system for last-mile access with a net transmission capacity of 40 Gbps is illustrated in this work. Orbital angular momentum (OAM) multiplexing has been integrated in the MMF-FSO transmission to augment the transmission speed and spectral efficiency of the system. Successful transmission along 100m MMF and 1200m FSO range is achieved with good system performance.

articleTitle: Inverse design of SOI-based angled multimode interferometer wavelength division (de)multiplexers
abstract: Angled multimode interferometers (AMMIs) offer an option for engineering optical dispersion for the wavelength division multiplexer. We propose and present experimental measurements for a prototype inverse-design two-port AMMI on the silicon-on-insulator (SOI) platform.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of Quantum-Dash Mode-locked Lasers for Optical Network Systems
abstract: The performance of InP/InAs quantum dash (QDash) multi-wavelength lasers is improved through modification of the growth scheme. We demonstrate that high performance QDash lasers exhibit high quality constellation diagrams at 32 GBaud 16QAM base-band signal.

articleTitle: Top-Surface Morphology Control of AlGaN Nanowires by Selective Area Epitaxy for Ultraviolet Nanophotonic Devices
abstract: In this paper, we report ultraviolet-emitting aluminum gallium nitride nanowires by selective area epitaxy with a controlled top-surface morphology as a promising platform for the development of ultraviolet nanophotonic devices.

articleTitle: Excess noise characterization of all-silicon avalanche photodetectors for telecommunication bandwidths
abstract: High-speed avalanche photodetectors are an important component due to the rapidly-growing demand for data rate. We demonstrate a monolithically integrated all-silicon avalanche photodetector for operation at 1550 nm. The internal gain is shown to be over 20 and the small signal bandwidth is measured to be 10 GHz. We present on a comprehensive study of the excess noise factor of the silicon avalanche photodiode. The excess noise factor is measured to fit a McIntyre model of k=0.10.

articleTitle: Towards Quantification of Images from Mouse, in-Vivo With Short-Wave Infrared Fluorescence
abstract: In pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, as two basis studies in pharmacology, measuring drug concentration over time is required. Conventional methods to measure drug concentration are invasive and time consuming. In this work, potential of fluorescent imaging at shortwave infrared as a real-time and non-invasive solution to extract the concentration of labeled drugs with fluorophore is demonstrated.

articleTitle: A New Method for Detection of Cerebral Aneurysm using Deep Learning
abstract: Currently, detection of aneurysms in the brain is a very actual topic. The brain aneurysm is a weak spot in the wall of a blood vessel inside the brain. In this paper, we will focus on different neural network architectures (2D CNN, 3D CNN, PointNet, …) for the detection and classification of aneurysms in the brain. In other words, the main goal of this paper is to create a system for detecting cerebral aneurysms to increase the overall accuracy of aneurysm detection by doctors.

articleTitle: Electro-optical terahertz imaging using a polarization image sensor
abstract: We report a novel terahertz imaging technique based on two-dimensional electro-optical sampling. A polarization image sensor is used to measure the spatially resolved polarization modulation of a probe beam. The temporal and spatial distribution of the terahertz electric field allow to obtain hyperspectral terahertz images in a simple and efficient way.

articleTitle: Metasurface Simplified Model for Lens Design Applications
abstract: We propose a workflow to introduce metasurfaces in optical design by using semi-analytical models. These models recover the output phase and polarization after propagation through the metasurface and can be used within optical design software. As such, metasurfaces can be optimized in optical systems by using built-in optimization processes while avoiding time-consuming electrodynamics computation. We present three variations of a triplet composed of a metasurface and refractive elements, all with similar optical performances.

articleTitle: Mode Division Multiplexing in Silicon Photonics for High-Speed Communication, Computation, and Quantum Information
abstract: In this presentation, we discuss challenges of calibrating and programming MZI-based programmable optical processors. We propose a novel architecture that tackles these issues, delivering faster and more energy-efficient programming while maintaining key performance metrics such as minimum insertion loss and resilience to fabrication imperfections.

articleTitle: Tuning the Optical Resonances in Plasmonic Nanostructured Arrays
abstract: We demonstrate optical coupling that arise from periodic arrays of gold NanoCubes (AuNC) grown atop a gold mirror allows us to independently control the two distinct optical modes, a plasmonic gap mode between the AuNC and the gold mirror surface and a surface lattice resonance mode (SRL). These devices will have applications in plasmonic lasing, enhanced photoluminescence and surface enhanced Raman scattering (SERS).

articleTitle: Individual Collagen Fibrils Investigated using Polarization-Resolved Second Harmonic Generation Microscopy
abstract: We investigate individual collagen fibrils using polarization SHG microscopy. It is found that polarization SHG is sensitive to changes in fibril structure caused by hydration, and changes in fibril out of plane orientation as a result of buckling.

articleTitle: Fabrication and characterization of terahertz zone plates based on foil stamping technique
abstract: We present a simple and inexpensive method for producing terahertz zone plates (THz-ZP) using the foil stamping technique. Two different zone plates as spiral zone plate (l=1) and Fresnel zone plate (l=0) were investigated and illustrated in both simulation and experiment. Both zone plates have a focal length of 50 mm in the operating frequency of 0.36 THz.

articleTitle: Hybrid Integration of Glass Materials with Silicon Photonics for Advanced Laser Applications
abstract: We review our recent progress in integration of rare-earth doped fiber amplifiers and chalcogenide micro-resonators with silicon photonic integrated circuits for multi-wavelength and tunable lasers in telecommunication and 2 micron spectral regions.

articleTitle: Matching emission and absorption profiles for improved performance in OPVs with perovskite nanoparticle down-converters
abstract: Due to the absorption-emission tunability by coexisting phases and cation replacement, perovskite nanoparticle synthesized by diblock copolymer micelles are down-conversion candidates for improved performance in organic photovoltaics by matching emission/ absorption profiles.

articleTitle: Scanless terahertz imaging in the time domain
abstract: We realize scanless time-domain imaging at terahertz frequencies, by combining a single-pixel imaging scheme with a “single-shot” detection method. We also apply compressed sensing to further speed up the acquisition process.

articleTitle: Thiol-Induced Dipole Effect on Gold Nanoparticles: A Study on the Optical Properties and Sensing Applications
abstract: In this study, we aim to investigate the nonlinearity of Au nanoparticles in rectennas, specifically when used as a near-infrared detector. We will focus on the effect of the SPR of Au nanoparticles on the nonlinearity of the rectenna, as well as the effect of dipole moment of the Au nanoparticles on the performance of the rectenna.

articleTitle: Ultra-Compact Silicon Photonic Interface for Satellite-to-Ground Downlinks
abstract: An ultra-compact array of optical antennas based on vertically coupled grating couplers has been designed to enable optical coupling with low geometrical losses. The array is followed by meshes of phase shifters and a binary tree of optical combiners to compensate for the phase fluctuations imposed on the beam’s wavefront due to atmospheric turbulence. The chip works as an intermediate level between free-space optics and fiber-based networks for satellite-to-ground downlinks and terrestrial optical wireless applications at 1550 nm wavelength.

articleTitle: Experimental separation estimation of incoherent optical sources reaching the (quantum) Cramér-Rao bound
abstract: Resolving light sources below the diffraction limit is a fundamental task both for astronomy and microscopy. Several recent works analysed this problem through the lens of quantum parameter estimation theory and proved that the separation between two point sources can be estimated at the quantum limit using intensity measurements after spatial-mode demultiplexing. We implement this technique and provide an optimal estimator based on a linear combination of demultiplexed intensity measurements [1–3]. Our experimental setup allows for the generation of the images of two sources, with tunable mutual coherence, as well as for spatial mode demultiplexing to estimate their separation [4].

articleTitle: Tuning of Exceptional-Point Microring Lasers Through Dual-Wavelength Coupler Design
abstract: We propose a fully integrated PT-symmetric laser based on two coupled microrings with saturable gain/loss. By using a dual wavelength coupler design, the device can operate in the vicinity of an exceptional point with low material gain, and without requiring independent control of the gain/loss in each resonator.

articleTitle: Vectorial Spin Hall Effect of Light upon Tight Focusing
abstract: Spin Hall effect of light is a manifestation of angular momentum conservation in the process of spin-orbit interaction of light. This effect is exhibited in tight focusing of a circularly polarized asymmetric input beam as a shift of the center of gravity of the focal spot in the transverse plane, perpendicular to the direction/axis of symmetry breaking. It is commonly established that the direction of this shift depends on the sign of the spin. We show, both analytically and by numerical simulation, that different Cartesian components of an asymmetric circularly polarized focused beam shift in opposite directions by different amounts. Moreover, these shifts depend on the type and degree of the asymmetry and thus can be tuned. We show how these field components’ shifts are related to spin and orbital angular momentum shifts. These findings shed new light on the spin optical Hall effect, facilitate new/simpler ways to measure it, and may broaden the gamut of its applications in manipulation and trapping of particles by light and precision metrology.

articleTitle: Comparison Between Kramers-Kronig and Self-coherent Transceivers for Free Space Optical Communications
abstract: Both Kramers-Kronig and self-coherent transceivers use a pilot carrier at the transmitter and as a result, the oscillator-signal mixing efficiency is much higher than coherent transceivers. However, Kramers-Kronig transceivers suffer from poor transmitter power efficiency while self-coherent transceivers require a larger receiver bandwidth due to heterodyne detection. The performance of Kramers-Kronig transceivers is better than self-coherent transceivers, provided that the pilot carrier power is sufficiently large.

articleTitle: Compressive real-time and ultrahigh-speed single-pixel imaging by swept aggregate patterns
abstract: We present a new technique for single-pixel imaging (SPI) capable of both ultrahigh-speed image acquisition and the real-time display of reconstructed images. Our approach combines a conventional digital micro-mirror device (DMD) with an off-the-shelf motorized polygonal mirror, achieving pattern projection rates of up to 14.1 MHz while still retaining the flexibility of DMD modulation with tunable frame sizes of up to $101 \times 103$ pixels. For real-time operation, we develop a lightweight reconstruction algorithm capable of compressed sensing that is compatible with parallel computation on a graphic processing unit (GPU). We show experimental demonstrations of offline ultrahigh-speed imaging at up to 12,000 frames per second (fps) and real-time streaming video at up to 100 fps.

articleTitle: Development of a Multifocal OCT Lens System and an Eye-Mimicking Phantom for Murine Eye Imaging
abstract: Retinal and vitreous imaging of the mouse eye can be used to study vascular retinal pathologies. This work presents a multifocal lens system allowing for deep axial field of view. To calibrate the lens system, an eye-mimicking optical phantom was developed and characterized. On this hemispherical phantom, an increase of averaged signal-to-noise ratio of 17 dB and averaged contrast improvement of 13 dB throughout the whole field of view were measured.

articleTitle: Real-time Optical Monitoring System Based on Frequency-to-Time Mapping Concept
abstract: Real-time optical monitoring of waveform frequency content with high speed will play a key role in future optical communication systems. Dispersive Fourier transformation (D-FTM) or frequency-to-time mapping method enables real-time spectral analysis of short isolated pulse-like signals but cannot be applied to continuous waveforms. Here, we propose, for the first time, a real-time optical monitoring (RTOM) system for dynamic spectral analysis of incoming telecommunication data streams over broad frequency bands, employing a temporal periodic sampling and dispersive delay scheme.

articleTitle: Spiral WBG based Ultra-compact Passive NOT Gate for High-speed Signals
abstract: We present a novel design for the realization of a fully-passive and linear NOT gate using a spiral waveguide Bragg grating (WBG) in an SOI platform. We demonstrated the inversion of a 50-Gbps NRZ-OOK data stream using the spiral WBG.

articleTitle: Parity-time symmetric Bragg gratings and directional couplers
abstract: Parity-time symmetric Bragg gratings produce unidirectional reflection around the exceptional point. A step-in-width Ag stripe waveguide with an IR-140 dye cover solution index-matched to the substrate is utilized to implement index and gain modulated Bragg gratings operating in the long-range surface plasmon mode. We investigate directional coupling between parity-time symmetric Bragg gratings near their exceptional point (□0 ~ ((0 nm), arranged as duplicate, duplicate-shifted, duplicate-flipped gratings, or involving a bus waveguide. Unidirectional multi-wavelength reflection and coupled supermode conversion are predicted.

articleTitle: Generation of single-mode few-cycle twin beams for time-domain quantum optics
abstract: Using a few-cycle femtosecond pulse with tailored group delay dispersion as the pump of a parametric down-conversion process, we produce bright entangled light pulses with more than 80% occupancy of a single temporal mode and a duration shorter than 4 optical cycles at near-infrared frequencies. Such states promise to open new opportunities in quantum metrology, such as subcycle sampling of mid-infrared quantum fields.

articleTitle: Local Oscillator Phase and Frequency Monitoring for Coherent Optical Spectrum Analyzer on a Chip
abstract: We demonstrate the silicon photonics implementation of a passive coherent discriminator based local oscillator phase and frequency monitoring stage for a coherent optical spectrum analyzer on a chip with minimal phase uncertainty.

articleTitle: Entanglement Distribution over Free-Space Optical Turbulent Channels
abstract: We demonstrate successful entanglement distribution over free-space optical link that we established at the University of Arizona in strong turbulence regime. To generate entangled photons, we use a low-cost solution based on a C-band laser diode and an EDFA as well as a PPLN waveguide in which wavelength conversion followed by spontaneous parametric downconversion takes place.

articleTitle: Spatial statistical analysis of deposition techniques for producing ordered nanoparticle arrays
abstract: Various solution-based deposition techniques were used to deposit reverse micelle templated nanoparticles to produce ordered arrangements. Presented here is a comparison of the two-dimensional dispersion using spatial statistical analysis to compare the spacing and lateral order of arrays produced by each technique.

articleTitle: Nonlinear topological photonics: from SSH to HOTIs
abstract: The Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) lattice represents a paradigmatic one-dimensional (1D) topological model, which has been widely employed in topological photonics and realized with versatile platforms including nanophotonics, plasmonics, and quantum optics [1–12]. In this talk, I will briefly discuss its topological nature and the new understanding of sub-symmetry protected topological states [13]. I will then focus on two examples from our recent work based on the 1D SSH photonic platform. One is in the fundamental side - about nonlinear control of topological edge states and tuning of parity-time symmetry using laser-written photonic lattices [10, 11]; the other is more towards application - about topologically tuned terahertz confinement in a nonlinear photonic chip [12]. Nonlinear control of topological states in higher-order topological insulators (HOTIs) will also be discussed, including the recent demonstrations of nonlinear control of photonic higher-order topological bound states in the continuum in two-dimensional SSH lattices [14] and nonlinearity-induced rotation of photonic p-orbital corner states in Kagome-type HOTIs [15]. I will end the talk with a brief outlook of topological photonics being an active field continuously in the coming decade [16].

articleTitle: D-HAN: An End-to-End Adaptive Neural Network for Snapshot Compressive Imaging
abstract: Snapshot compressive imaging (SCI) has surged as a crucial tool for data visualization in applications limited to a single-shot. However, most existing methods shortfall in the reiterated use of random coded apertures and the idealization of the shearing function behavior. To overcome these limitations, we develop a new end-to-end convolutional neural network, termed deep high-dimensional adaptive net (D-HAN), that supplies the SCI systems with multifaceted supervision in the encoding operation, the shearing process, and the reconstruction. D-HAN is implemented in a representative SCI system for hyperspectral and ultrahigh-speed imaging.

articleTitle: Chemical Imaging of Microparticles with Raman, FTIR and Quantum Cascade Laser Microscopy
abstract: Microplastic contamination of the environment and ecosystem has attracted much attention in recent years. Its presence has been detected in the most remote regions and its propagation through the food chain poses a serious health risk to humans and animals. To better understand their presence in the environment, their detection and identification plays a critical role in any remediation effort. FTIR and Raman imaging provide simultaneously size metrology and spectral information and have been gold standard tools for microplastic analysis. In this study, we will present state-of-the-art chemical imaging methods, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and Raman imaging as well as quantum cascade laser mapping, for the detection of microplastic particles. We will demonstrate enhanced detection through the use of reflective substrates and discuss the signal enhancement strategies of these chemical imaging techniques as well as their limitations.

articleTitle: Core-Shell Perovskite-TiO2 Nanoparticles for High Stability
abstract: In recent years, hybrid halide perovskite nanostructures have gained traction for their optoelectronic properties. Their application, however, is hindered by their instability to moisture, oxygen, and UV radiation. To overcome this issue, we are reporting a method to produce perovskites capped with TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> to form highly stable core-shell nanoparticles. The TiO2 shell protects the perovskites from environmental degradation, with broad emission.

articleTitle: Surface Plasmon Optoelectronics
abstract: Plasmonic nanostructures and metasurfaces offer a new paradigm for the design of optoelectronic devices. We discuss nanoscale device ideas that exploit the optical field enhancement and confinement provided by such structures to achieve performance benefits or enable new functionalities.

articleTitle: Impact of GaN μLEDs aspect ratio on bandwidth and efficiency
abstract: Gallium Nitride (GaN) microLEDs have received a lot of attention in the field of microdisplays due to their interesting properties, such as high luminosity and robustness, and they are also gaining interest in the field of Visible Light Communication (VLC). With this increasing interest, studying carrier dynamics in these devices is crucial to understand how the recombination mechanisms affect their performance. In this paper, we quantify the effect of perimeter over surface ratio on the performance of Multiple-Quantum-Wells InGaN/GaN μLEDs.

articleTitle: Ultrafast Yb:KGW laser pumped at 946 nm
abstract: The development of an efficient ultrashort pulse Yb:KGW laser oscillator pumped by a Nd:YAG laser is reported. The pump source was a 10 W Nd:YAG laser operating at 946 nm. In the mode-locked regime, 139 fs long pulses at 1028 nm were generated at a repetition rate of 54.6 MHz with an average output power of up to 0.86 W, corresponding to optical-to-optical efficiency of 27.2% with respect to the absorbed pump power.

articleTitle: Development of AI tools for assessing the pain state of a mouse
abstract: The Mouse Grimace Scale (MGS) [1] has emerged as a valuable tool for pain assessment in mice by analyzing facial features. This study aims to automate and enhance this process through the development of an innovative image capture system, utilizing near-infrared (NIR) spectrum illumination for less intrusive and clearer facial images. Real-time pain assessment is achieved by precise segmentation of the eye, ear, and muzzle areas using fine-tuned Mask R-CNN. Furthermore, a comprehensive dataset of over 3000 high-quality images, created by us, was employed for training and validation, resulting in improved accuracy and reliability of our pain evaluation system. These contributions not only advance the field of pain evaluation in mice but also address a limitation in a previous study that solely focused on assessing pain based on the eye area [2]. By incorporating additional facial regions, our approach provides a more comprehensive understanding of pain manifestations in mice, enabling a more nuanced and accurate assessment. These findings open up new avenues for further research and development in pain evaluation methodologies.

articleTitle: Ambipolar Photoelectric Devices with GaN/InGaN Nanowire Heterojunctions
abstract: In this work, we report ambipolar photo-electrochemistry based photoelectric devices with epitaxial semiconductor n-GaN/p-InGaN nanowire heterojunctions.

articleTitle: Non-Hermitian Topological Photonics Beyond the Tight-Binding Regime
abstract: Topological photonics is well studied in Hermitian systems. In these systems, the tight-binding model is the main tool of exploration. This model is however not well suited for Non-Hermitian systems due to the effect of long-range couplings. In this work, we look at topological photonics in Non-Hermitian systems and go beyond the tight-binding regime. We investigated a dimerized plasmonic chain beyond the quasistatic limit, using their resonances - Quasinormal Modes (QNMs) - as the fundamental machinery of exploration.

articleTitle: Plastic particles detection in animal flour using continuous terahertz waves
abstract: We have demonstrated the feasibility of terahertz (THz) frequency-domain spectroscopy to detect plastic contaminants in animal flour. The flour was held between two plastic membranes and different plastic contents were introduced into the sample while keeping the same weight. Free standing powder with and without contaminant samples were characterized using a compact continuous wave (CW) THz system. The variation of the transmission as a function of different plastic content in the samples were experimentally demonstrated. This work paves the way for the development of in-situ testing of food contaminants in animal flour using THz waves.

articleTitle: Design of an Integrated Multi-Band Continuous Optical Filter using Mechanical Tuning
abstract: Multi-band tunable optical filters in telecommunications can significantly improve the performance and capacity of optical communication networks by improving the optical spectrum's efficiency. Moreover, dynamically tuning filter bandwidths can further improve efficiency and flexibility. This paper presents a novel approach to designing optical filters that selectively pass or block multi-wavelength bands of the input spectrum.

articleTitle: Post-fabrication resonance trimming technique compatible with state-of-the-art foundry technology
abstract: Silicon photonics is widely received as the next-generation technology in telecommunications and data interconnects. The high standards in on-chip signal processing require very precise control over the device parameters which is jeopardized by fabrication variabilities. We demonstrate a resonance trimming technique which allows the resonance wavelength of a ring filter to be accurately modified. A 760-pm modification was achieved on a single-bus 4-ring cascaded optical filter.

articleTitle: Fusion of Photonics & Semiconductor for Industry 4.0
abstract: the author addresses three key trends in the fusion of photonics & semiconductor migrating from optical interconnect to photonic integrated circuit, from 3D to 4D integration, and from simple device to microsystem. The changes will create a paradigm shift for the industry ecosystem in the next decade and beyond.

articleTitle: High Data Throughput Wireless Networks Based on a Quantum Dash / Dot Multi-Wavelength Laser and Millimeter-Wave-Over-Fiber Transmission Links
abstract: We have designed, epitaxy-grown, nano-fabricated and investigated several different-type InAs/InP quantum dash / dot (QD) multi-wavelength lasers (MWLs) around 1550 nm with very low relative intensity noise and ultra-narrow optical linewidth. By using those QD MWLs, we have experimentally demonstrated optical-heterodyne millimeter-wave-over-fiber fronthaul systems with high data throughput wireless links through 25- and 50-km single mode fiber featuring a free-space data capacity of up to 36 Gb/s, which has clearly indicated that the developed QD MWLs are critical building blocks of achieving low-noise millimeter-wave (mmW) signal generation and transmission for 5G & beyond wireless networks.

articleTitle: Dual-Dispersive Compressive Spectral Structured Light Imaging
abstract: Spectral depth imaging (SDI) based on active illumination is an advanced computer vision approach for monitoring/detection applications. Structured-light (SL)-based SDIs have become popular due to their high accuracy and low-complexity setups. However, recent approaches rely on expensive color or multispectral filter arrays that limit their spectral resolution. To overcome these limitations, we develop a structured light-based SDI, termed compact compressive spectral depth imager (CoCOSDI) that offers high-dimensional encoding by synergistically combining inexpensive color/binary films and a direct vision prism.

articleTitle: Terahertz Components Through Additive Manufacturing
abstract: The Collier Research Group is focused on terahertz (THz) photonics [1]-[2], spectroscopy [3], spectral imaging [4]-[5], optofluidics [6], and microfluidics [7]. In this invited talk, we will discuss our recent advancements in THz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) of additive manufacturing materials [3] and investigations of THz components fabricated with additive manufacturing [8].

articleTitle: Towards Combinational Logic Circuits based on Optical Logic Gates
abstract: An optical universal logic gate is experimentally demonstrated. A cascade of two MZI-based thermo-optic switches independently controlled with on-off-keying (OOK) achieves a NOR logic function for combinational logic circuits with a high contrast ratio of 27.9 dB and insertion loss of 0.5 dB. The fabricated device is a building block towards an all-optical SR-latch circuit.

articleTitle: Nanostructured Organic Optoelectronics Revisited
abstract: The implementation of nanostructures in optoelectronic devices has been studied extensively with the aim of light management and device efficiency enhancement. Here we discuss recent advances. We focus on the effect of nanopatterns integrated with solar cells and photodetectors based on organic semiconductor materials (OPV). We present finite-element method (FEM) simulations to calculate the wavelength- and angle-resolved effects of nanostructures on the photocurrent. We demonstrate that the effect of the nanostructure is low in wavelength ranges where the material’s absorption is high, while it has a high benefit where the absorption is low. There it may be used to realize narrowband absorption enhancement. We validate the impact of the optical resonance effects on the electrical device characteristics experimentally.

articleTitle: Dual-line c-cut Nd:YVO laser
abstract: Dual-wavelength operation of a c-cut Nd:YVO laser at 1062/1066.6 nm was demonstrated by using a birefringent filter. The maximum output power of 300 mW for 800 mW of pump power was obtained.

articleTitle: Compressive Spectral Video via Wavelength-Dynamic Coded Aperture
abstract: Compressive spectral video (CSV) has emerged as a novel research topic in computer vision, having powerful implications in retrieving a four-dimensional tensor from a reduced set of two-dimensional compressed measurements. The advances in CSV architectures have shown that the recovery of four-dimensional data is possible, but the quality is still far from the requirements of real applications. To overcome these limitations, this work analyses the parameter design of a novel dynamic spectro-temporal encoding methodology based on a digital micromirror device sync with a tunable filter.

articleTitle: Comparison between Homodyne and PNR Detection Schemes for Quantum Key Distribution
abstract: In this paper, we study the comparison between two different methods of detection regarding key generation rate in a quantum key distribution system. We illustrate that after a threshold PNR detection outperforms homodyne detection.

articleTitle: Attosecond photoelectron spectroscopy using high-harmonic generation and seeded free-electron lasers
abstract: In this work, we use attosecond time-resolved techniques to investigate photoionization dynamics on its natural timescale, employing both high harmonic generation and seeded free-electron lasers to generate extreme ultraviolet attosecond pulse trains for our studies. With the former approach, we examine the role of nuclear motion in molecular photoionization dynamics, while with the latter we introduce a novel attosecond timing tool for single-shot characterization of the relative phase between the XUV and the infrared field.

articleTitle: Femtosecond Yb:CALGO laser operating at 8 MHz
abstract: We have demonstrated a mode-locked Yb:CALGO laser operating at 8.2 MHz repetition rate. The cavity was extended based on the White cell configuration which consists of 3 concave mirrors and is easy to control to change the cavity length. We got 126 fs pulses by using a 10% output coupler. The output power was 430 mW at 21 W of incident pump power. The corresponding pulse energy was 52 nJ and the peak power was 416 kW.

articleTitle: Video-rate multi-scale band-limited illumination profilometry with cubic-meter-level measurement volume
abstract: We have developed multi-scale band-limited illumination profilometry (MS-BLIP), for robust video-rate three-dimensional (3D) imaging over measurement volumes at the cubic meter (m$^{3}$) level. MS-BLIP applies a newly developed iterative method for distortion compensation, which empowers a dynamic 3D visualization with a measurement volume of up to 1.5 m$^{3}$. It can robustly resolve spatially isolated objects with varied reflectance. It also allows flexible adjustment of the orientation of the field of view with a dove prism. MSBLIP showcases the video-rate 3D surface imaging of full human-body movements.

articleTitle: Divide and Focus by Breaking Symmetry and Creating a New One: Generation of and Simple Switching Between Novel Focal Modalities by Phase Splitting the Incoming Beam
abstract: We show that by phase-splitting a beam, there appear novel features upon its focusing by a cylindrical lens: a transverse dark line and a longitudinally polarized transverse line. Switching between these modalities is achieved by an incoming linear polarization 90° rotation. We interpret these findings as a requirement to transform the symmetry of the incoming polarization to match that of the field to be generated in the focus. This scheme may find applications in microscopy, probing anisotropic media, particle manipulation.

articleTitle: Integrated distributed Bragg reflector lasers in silicon nitride waveguides coated with erbium-doped tellurite
abstract: In this work, we show on-chip distributed Bragg reflector lasers in 200-nm-thick silicon nitride waveguides coated with erbium-doped tellurium dioxide. The devices consist of asymmetrical cavities defined by sidewall corrugations patterned directly on 2.2-cm-long silicon nitride waveguides. The lasers operate within the C-band (1530-1565 nm) with highly directional output and efficiencies up to 0.36% and lasing threshold as low as 13 mW when pumped with 1470 nm light.

articleTitle: Surface photo voltage spectroscopy: a powerful technique for characterization of materials and devices
abstract: Surface Photovoltage Spectroscopy (SPS) has become an important tool for the characterization of semiconductor materials. Results obtained in the characterization of MoO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> thin films grown onto silicon substrates are presented. We report on an original application of SPS to monitoring the different texturing and passivation processes in manufacturing crystalline silicon solar cells. Results highlight the potentialities of SPS as a simple, contactless, and non-destructive tool for the characterization of semiconductors structures and solar cell devices, allowing to obtain energy transitions, and serving as a guidance in monitoring texturing and passivation processes in solar cells fabrication without the necessity of depositing metal contacts.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of InAs/InP Quantum Dash/Dot Mode-locked Lasers
abstract: The performance of InP/InAs quantum dash (QDash) and quantum dot (QDot) multi-wavelength lasers, using identical structural design, are investigated and compared to each other. The QDash lasers show a lower threshold current and cavity loss. On the other hand, the QDot lasers show higher internal quantum efficiency, as well as lower average integrated relative intensity noise (RIN) and average optical linewidth. This finding highlights the viability of InAs/InP QDash/QDot lasers to be used as a low-cost optical source for large-scale networks.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Enabled Inverse Design of Subwavelength Waveguide Gratings using Environment-Aware Effective Medium Approximations
abstract: Accurate design of complex grating structures using 3D simulations is computationally intensive. Our ultimate goal is to create a 2D effective index model of a 3D subwavelength waveguide structure to carry out inverse design of the device with accuracies comparable to 3D simulations. Here we present a deep neural network surrogate model to predict the optical response of the 2D effective structure as a first step.

articleTitle: Single-Shot Ultrafast Photography with Terahertz Waves
abstract: We demonstrate a single-shot ultrafast terahertz photography system that can capture multiple frames of a complex ultrafast scene in non-transparent media with sub-picosecond temporal resolutions. By multiplexing an optical probe beam in the time and spatial-frequency domains simultaneously, we encode the terahertz-captured spatiotemporal dynamics into distinct spatial-frequency regions of a multiplexed image, which is then computationally decoded and reconstructed.

articleTitle: Multistability in a nonlinear THz split ring resonator
abstract: We analyze diverse tuning regions of a single nonlinear split-ring resonator (NSRR) and reveal different regions where multistability can be found. This exciting dynamical behavior of the NSRR is carried out using two-parameter sweep diagrams in an appropriate range. In the multistable regions, the NSRR model exhibits strong sensitivity to initial conditions, and hysteretic behaviors, demonstrating the presence of coexisting patterns. We exploited a cross-section of the basin of attraction to locate two coexisting behaviors. Such behavior is an important feature for photonic memory devices.

articleTitle: Development of spiropyran-doped poly(dimethylsiloxane) optical waveguides for sensing applications
abstract: In this work, we describe the incorporation of spiropyrans (SP) in PDMS for the fabrication of photochromic optical waveguides. We show that adequate SP selection is important for the fabrication of optically transparent PDMS waveguides with low propagation loss, and that the incorporated dyes preserved their photochromic properties.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Properties of Hybrid ZnTe-on-Si Waveguides for Telecommunication Applications
abstract: Nonlinear photonic devices are critical for many integrated infrared platform applications such as supercontinuum generation and frequency combs. It also holds the promise of all-optical modulators that will surpass by orders of magnitude the current devices. Typically, these devices rely on Si material platforms that suffer from high nonlinear losses due to two-photon absorption (TPA). A novel, hybrid ZnTe-on-Si waveguide system is demonstrated and fully characterized via ellipsometry and a combination of a bidirectional top-hat spectral broadening measurement and a dispersive scan (D-Scan) experiment to extract the effective TPA coefficient ($\beta_{TPA}$) and optical Kerr coefficient (n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) of the hybrid waveguide system. The experimentally characterized $\beta_{TPA}$=S.76x1$0^{-13}$m/W of this ZnTe-on-Si system is an order of magnitude lower than pure Si waveguides with a comparable nonlinear Kerr coefficient, providing a promising material platform for future high-performance, low-loss, compact, integrated nonlinear infrared devices.

articleTitle: Tunable Hybrid Plasmonic-Semiconductor Laser Incorporating ENZ Material
abstract: In this paper, we suggest a new approach to achieve tunability in semiconductor lasers, based on mode loss perturbation. We propose a hybrid plasmonic-semiconductor laser, in which we add a metal oxide semiconductor (MOS) on top of a conventional Fabry-Perot (FP) InP-based diode laser. This hybrid laser experiences significant change in the imaginary part of the mode effective index when the MOS operates in the accumulation region, which constitutes the basis of our tuning mechanism.

articleTitle: Quantum Dash Optical Frequency Comb Sources for Optical Communications and Microwave Photonics
abstract: We review recent work on developing quantum dash optical frequency comb sources for applications on coherent WDM transmission as well as microwave photonic signal processing, including filtering and photonic beamforming.

articleTitle: Quantum Carrier Modeling for Gate-tunable Plasmonic
abstract: The voltage-tunable carrier density profile (n) of an Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) layer, incorporated as a semiconductor layer in a metal-oxide-semiconductor (MOS) capacitor, is computed via the conventional drift-diffusion (CDD) and Schrödinger-Poisson coupling (SP) models. Under accumulation, the SP model predicts a bump in n which is significantly different from the CDD result. Increasing the voltage switches the real part of permittivity from positive to negative in a region within ITO, creating a metallic layer bounded by epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) point(s). This result has significant implications for plasmonic devices implemented with ENZ materials in a MOS structure.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Soliton Microcombs via Genetic Algorithms
abstract: We illustrate a novel strategy to robustly generate combs in microring resonators pumped with a continuous-wave laser source, by employing genetic algorithms to optimize the parameters required for coherent state generation.

articleTitle: Lifetime and Photosensitivity in Laser Exposed TFSI-Treated MoS2
abstract: 2D semiconductors such as MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> hold promise for next generation optoelectronics. However, their low photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) inhibits their industrial use. Chemical treatments including trifluoromethansulfonimide (TFSI) acid have demonstrated PLQY enhancement up to near unity but struggle with consistency within literature. We demonstrate laser light exposure over large time scales (5 hours) is responsible for discrepancies in photoluminescence (PL) enhancement factors. A 74X enhancement of photoluminescence intensity is observed in TFSI-treated MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> with corresponding increases in carrier lifetimes.

articleTitle: Highly Efficient Ultra-Broad Beam Silicon Nanophotonic Antenna for Two-Dimensional Optical Phased Arrays
abstract: we demonstrate a novel design of an ultracompact silicon grating antenna for off-chip light emission, with an unprecedented performance combining a wide far-field beam width of 52° and 62°, a very compact footprint of $3.1 \mu \mathrm{m}\times 1.7 \mu \mathrm{m}$, and a high diffraction efficiency of 82% after incorporating a bottom reflector for improved directionality. This is achieved by a single-etch grating structure and a Bragg reflector designed on a 300-nm-thick SOI platform.

articleTitle: Waveguide Taper Profile Optimization for Compact On-chip Adiabatic Devices
abstract: We review our waveguide taper profile optimization method for adiabatic integrated optical devices. We demonstrate a length reduction of fiber-to-chip light couplers, power splitters, and mode converters by factors ranging from 2 to 5 compared to their linear counterparts while achieving low losses and large bandwidth.

articleTitle: Characterization of Active Liquid Crystal With Continuous Terahertz Waves
abstract: We have demonstrated an active liquid crystal (LC) device operating in the terahertz (THz) frequency range. The device consists of LCs placed between glass plates with electrodes. Liquid crystals (LCs) are good materials for active phase and bias devices. Using a compact continuous wave (CW) THz system, our experimental results confirmed the phase variation due to the mechanical rotation of the LC or to the bias voltage varying from 0 to 30 V applied between the electrodes at different frequencies. This work opens a simple path towards the development of active THz liquid crystal devices to serve as low-cost phase plates.

articleTitle: Transient absorption analysis of Au nanoparticles on glass and FTO:glass substrates
abstract: In this work, we present the formation of Au nanoparticles on glass and FTO: glass substrate by magnetron sputtering followed by the thermal dewetting process. The surface morphology and absorption spectra are measured using scanning electron microscopy and ultraviolet-visible spectroscopy respectively. The charge carrier dynamics of as-fabricated Au nanoislands are discussed based on their transient absorption measurements.

articleTitle: Soliton trapping and harmonic oscillations due to nonlinear interactions in optical fibers
abstract: When the fiber dispersion is normal, there exists a pair of bright and dark solitons with orthogonal polarizations. When the power of the dark soliton (pump) on one polarization is stronger than that of the bright pulse (signal) on the other polarization, we found that the bright pulse is trapped into the dip of the dark soliton, and it undergoes harmonic oscillations if the mean frequency of the bright pulse is lower than a certain critical frequency. Otherwise, it escapes the potential well formed by the dark soliton. Analytical expressions derived for the frequency of harmonic oscillations and the asymptotic value of the trapped energy are in good agreement with numerical experiments. This result could have potential applications for ultra-fast all-optical switching and logic gates.

articleTitle: PeakForce Quantitative Nanomechanical Information for Reverse Micelle Synthesis
abstract: PeakForce Quantitative Nanomechanical Mapping (QNM), an atomic force microscopy (AFM) technique that extracts quantitative material property data, was applied to study the infiltration of precursor salts into di-block copolymer reverse micelles to better understand nanoparticle formation. Based on the Young’s modulus map obtained, the relative micelle modulus (unloaded vs loaded) was found to increase with the amount of salt loading. This provides critical in-situ insight into the formation of controllable nanoparticle patterns for energy, biosensing, and optics applications.

articleTitle: Advances in machine learning-based design for high-volume manufacturing of planar lightwave circuits
abstract: The increasing functionality and associated complexity of planar lightwave circuits demand novel approaches to the design and simulation of photonic chips. In high-volume manufacturing, it is critical that photonic circuits are designed in ways that can withstand inevitable process variations. We discuss our use of machine learning and deep neural networks to advance the design and fabrication of optical chips in a high-volume production environment. We also describe the capabilities of our silica-on-silicon planar lightwave circuit platform and its exceptional characteristics that make it essential for the realization of key building blocks in LiDAR and optical coherence tomography systems.

articleTitle: Compact and Broadband Inverse Taper-based Light Couplers with Optimized Profiles
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate an optimized, inverse polynomial taper profile Si light coupler. Coupling losses of 0.5 dB and 0.8 dB were measured at 1550 nm for the TE and TM modes for a 15 $\mu$m long device with a broadband response.

articleTitle: Silicon Reconfigurable Optical Logic Using Phase-Change Materials
abstract: We present the use of an optical phase change material to create scalable and reconfigurable optical logic switches. We demonstrate that two logic operations can be achieved at a single wavelength using a single microdisk; while dual nanobeams in a Mach-Zehnder configuration could realize a resonant bistable crossbar switch. More complex logic functions can be obtained by introducing multiple stage cascaded microdisks or Mach-Zehner networks. This work suggests alternative switch configurations in silicon photonics.

articleTitle: Preparation and characterization of a photovoltaic solar cell with poly(3-hexylthiophene) and fullerene (C60) as active materials.
abstract: Solar photovoltaics present a reliable alternative to global energy problems. In recent years, researchers have turned to organic solar cells. These types of solar cells are low pollutant, inexpensive, flexible etc. We developed an organic solar cell with polymer as active materials, poly(3-hexylthiophene) PAT6 and fullerene (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</inf>). PAT6 is a N type material and therefore an electron donor and C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</inf> is a P type material and therefore an electron acceptor. They are also highly absorbent in ultraviolet thus promoting the process of generating peer electron-hole in the cell. PAT6 is deposited by the sol-gel deposition technique on C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</inf> developed by thermal evaporation under vacuum. Different thicknesses of the PAT6 layer were studied to assess their impacts on the semiconducting properties of the cell. Tin oxide and indium (ITO) electrodes were used. The photovoltaic properties of the ITO/C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</inf>/PAT6/ITO cell were improved by the introduction of buffers of molybdenum oxide (MoO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) and zinc oxide (ZnO) as electrons and holes transport layers to the respective electrodes. The absorptions evaluated using the Cary 5000 spectrophotometer show that our cells are absorbing in much of the visible spectrum and in ultraviolet.

articleTitle: Real-time spectral characterization of THz-bandwidth waveforms by unwrapping a time-lens spectrogram
abstract: We experimentally show a spectral unwrapping algorithm to analyze ultra-broadband signals using the time-lens spectrogram. By using a spectrogram with a nominal analysis bandwidth of only 56.4 GHz, we show that the analysis bandwidth can be continuously shifted to analyze a waveform with 1.97 THz bandwidth, akin to the principle of down-conversion employed in RF spectral analyzers. This allows us to obtain time-resolved spectra extending over long durations with high resolution in a single-shot manner.

articleTitle: Optimization of Polarization-Independent Chand-Bali Nano-antenna for Energy Harvesting
abstract: We propose a novel Chand-Bali nano-antenna that uses a gradient-based optimization method to achieve polarization-independent operation in the infrared range, specifically at 10.6 μm. The optimized design allows for wide-angle reception. The nano-antenna is made up of two elliptical metallic resonators, one of which has an elliptic cut. It serves as the top layer of a metal-insulator-metal (MIM) structure, which allows for easy formation of thin insulator layers in the gap of the metallic resonators, creating an infrared energy harvester rectenna. The strong confinement of the electric field in the gap improves the performance of MIM rectifiers. Our simulations indicate that this design is well suited for energy harvesting and detection, and can be scaled to different wavelengths.

articleTitle: Investigating the Crystalline Structure of Collagen-like Fibrils within Inner Ear Crystals by Second Harmonic Generation Microscopy
abstract: Polarization-resolved SHG (PSHG) microscopy imaging was performed to determine PSHG parameters related to the ultrastructure of the collagen-like protein matrix embedded in mammalian inner ear crystals.

articleTitle: Far-Infrared Bragg Device
abstract: Terahertz (THz) science and photonics utilize the far-infrared electromagnetic spectrum within the approximate wavelength range of 30 μm to 3000 μm—corresponding to a frequency range of 0.1 THz to 10 THz [1]. These THz frequencies (formally known as the THz gap) were challenging to generate and detect before the advent of modern THz technologies, such as THz photoconductive antennas and electro-optic detectors, which are now widespread in THz devices. Advancement of THz science and photonics is being continued through on-going development of experimental THz devices. Various experimental THz device designs are leveraging additive manufacturing (i.e., three-dimensional printing technology) for fabrication with THz compatible materials and novel geometries [2]. In this paper, we summarize the frequency response of our recently-developed far-infrared Bragg device [3]—fabricated with additive manufacturing.

articleTitle: Bidirectional RoF 5G Fronthaul Transmission Links with an InAs/InP Quantum Dash Laser
abstract: We have experimentally demonstrated a bidirectional radio-over-fiber (RoF) 5G new radio (NR) fronthaul transmission link based on an InAs/InP quantum dash mode-locked laser (QD-MLL), which provide low noise and highly coherent optical carriers. Two of the optical carriers are used for heterodyne based millimeter wave (MMW) RoF downlink transmission. The signal of the downlink is a 2-GBaud 16-QAM signal located at 28.951 GHz after heterodyne detection. The third optical carrier is used in uplink. The signal used in the uplink is a 2-GBaud 16-QAM signal located at 4 GHz. The result is verified by error-vector-magnitude (EVM) in real-time. The EVM of the downlink and uplink is up to 9.5% and 7.9% respectively in back-to-back setup.

articleTitle: Direct Intensity Detection of QAM Telecommunications Signals
abstract: We report a new method for recovering QAM telecommunications signals using time-frequency analysis provided by a time-lens spectrogram comprising of electro-optic phase modulation and dispersive propagation. This method requires only a single photodiode in the detection stage, avoiding the need for a phase locked local oscillator. Using a simple decision algorithm to recover phase-only symbol transitions in real-time, we demonstrate the decoding of a 1 Gbaud/s QAM4 signal with pre-FEC BER $\lt 5.96 \times {10}^{-8}$ without any coherent detection or interferometric system.

articleTitle: QKD Over FSO Under Different Weather Conditions Using OptiSystem Software
abstract: OptiSystem software is used to implement BB84 QKD protocol and enable transmission of coded bits over FSO channel. The effect of the weather condition on the performance of the BB84 QKD system is investigated. QBER performance metric is used to measure the QKD system.

articleTitle: Pulse-to-Pulse Stability Comparison Between 810 1030 and 1064nm Pulsed Laser
abstract: We present a pulse-to-pulse (P2P) stability comparison between three different kinds of laser. The first laser is a Ti: sapphire laser operating at 810nm spectral region. The second laser is an Ytterbium-doped (YDF) pulsed fiber laser working at 1030nm which its bandwidth generated directly at the seed laser. The third laser is an YDF pulsed fiber laser operating at 1064nm which its spectrum is broadened in the amplifier stages due to the self-phase modulation (SPM). P2P fluctuation of 2, 2.8 and 3.4 percent are achieved respectively for original wavelength of 1030, 810 and 1064nm pulsed lasers. Furthermore, P2P fluctuation of 4.3, 14.5 and 16.3 percent are achieved respectively for SHG signals of 1030, 1064 and 810nm pulsed lasers.

articleTitle: Low repetition rate Yb-doped all-fiber Mamyshev oscillator
abstract: We have developed a fiber Mamyshev oscillator with a sub-MHz fundamental repetition rate that generates 20 nJ femtosecond pulses at 1030 nm. To achieve such a low repetition rate, a 100-m linear cavity in combination with two chirped fiber Bragg gratings for dispersion compensation were required. Lower repetition rates should be achievable by adjusting the parameters of the laser cavity. Such a laser used as a seed could replace pre-amplification and pulse-picking stages in chirped-pulse amplification systems.

articleTitle: Noise modelling using Deep CNN for Terahertz Super-Resolution Imaging
abstract: This work focuses on a generalized noise model for terahertz imaging. Statistical noise masks are constructed to analyze Gaussian, quantization, data-drop and speckle noises in terahertz images, and are analyzed using the Noise2Clean algorithm. The consensus of the Noise2Noise algorithm is also analyzed to obtain super-resolution with only noisy data. The results show that a deep convolution network can be trained using numerical probability distribution models for denoising terahertz images with only noisy training samples.

articleTitle: Vortex Beams on Incoherent Background
abstract: We introduce a novel class of structured random beams carrying orbital angular momentum on incoherent background. We confirm that such beams maintain their vortex structure in free space and manifest robust behavior against atmospheric turbulence as well.

articleTitle: Self-assembled templated Metal/Metal Oxide nano-junctions: A new approach to the Purple of Cassius
abstract: Self-assembled spherical reverse micelles formed using diblock copolymers, specifically PS-b-P2VP, were used to grow SnO2 nanoparticles decorated with Au, exploiting the spontaneous reaction between SnCl2 and HAuCl4. The use of reverse micelles enables uniformity in size and dispersion of nanoparticles. This route leads to nanoparticles with tunable optical and magnetic properties with respect to the ratio of SnO2 and Au. XPS analysis also reveals a higher amounts of gold oxide in the composite nanoparticle suggesting their suitability for redox gas sensing.

articleTitle: Narrow spectral bandwidth passively mode-locked pulsed fiber system at 1030 nm
abstract: We report the generation of narrow spectral bandwidth, high energy pulses using a narrow bandwidth fiber bragg grating. To limit the spectral broadening due to nonlinear effects a large core diameter gain fiber is adopted. The spectral bandwidth of 0.07 nm is obtained for 280 ps pulses with pulse energy of 1.6$\mu$J at a repetition rate of 6.28 MHz, corresponding to average output power of 10.2 W and 5.5 kW of peak power.

articleTitle: Efficiently Harvesting Infrared Energy: An Optimization Strategy for Rectenna Design
abstract: In this study, we propose an optimization strategy for designing efficient rectennas for harvesting infrared (IR) energy. The rectenna is primarily composed of a rectifying component, such as a diode, and an antenna. In the IR range, the ultra-high frequency alternating current signal captured by the antenna terminals must be transformed into a useful direct current signal efficiently. The metal-insulator-metal (MIM) diode, due to its ultra-fast quantum tunneling as a conduction mechanism, is the most suitable option for operation in these IR ranges. Matching the impedance between the antenna and the diode, addressing the nonlinearity of the diode, and dealing with the effect of capacitance on the device's cutoff frequency are challenges that need to be overcome to achieve an efficient rectenna. An optimization algorithm is applied to enhance the rectenna's performance by taking into consideration these challenges.

articleTitle: 112 Gbps integrated single mode fiber-free space optics transmission enabled by polarization division multiplexing for last-mile access networks
abstract: The integration of a single mode fiber (SMF) and free-space-optics (FSO) link for providing high-speed data services to last-mile end users is illustrated in this work. 112 Gbps data along 50 km SMF and 1400 m FSO range is transported by integrating polarization-division-multiplexing (PDM) and 16level-quadrature amplitude modulation (16-QAM) signals with in-phase quadrature (IQ) modulation. Digital signal processing (DSP) algorithms are incorporated for compensation of channel losses.

articleTitle: Self-Healing Capabilities of Airy Beams on Incoherent Background: Experimental Investigation
abstract: We report an experimental realization of recently introduced Airy beams on incoherent background (ABIBs), which are structured random beams capable of defying diffraction in free space. We demonstrate that the laboratory realizations of ABIBs are capable of self-healing after having been obstructed by defects which make them attractive to optical communications, optical imaging, and information transfer applications.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Optics in a Diamond Micro- and Nano-Cavities
abstract: Resonant recirculation of light in optical microcavities can greatly enhance light-matter interactions. In this work, we demonstrate cavity-enhanced second-harmonic and third-harmonic generation from a single-crystal diamond microdisk. The presence of crystal defects – here nitrogen-vacancy centers – breaks the inversion symmetry of the diamond crystal, allowing for observation of the otherwise forbidden second-harmonic generation. We further show that the photon emission follows a clear dependency with cavity detuning of both the pump and emission modes, a clear indication of a doubly-resonant configuration.

articleTitle: InSb-based THz Plasmonic Antenna for Dynamic Control of Radiative decay rate of Quantum emitters
abstract: We propose an InSb-based THz plasmonic antenna capable of dynamically tuning the radiative decay rate of an electric dipole emitter upon magnetization. The magnetized antenna supports magnetoplasmon modes that can radiatively couple to the transition dipole moment of the dipole source, resulting in multiband radiative decay rate enhancement. This proposed system holds great potential to realize tunable single photon sources with high saturation intensity in the THz regime.

articleTitle: Core-shell nanoparticles by reverse micelle templating as potential optical isolators
abstract: Using reverse micelle templating as a universal route for nanoparticles, we have been able to produce various core-shell nanoparticle structures with interesting magnetooptical effects. Both polymer and Au shells around a metal oxide core have shown unusual magneto-optical properties. By exploiting the magnetic properties of the nanoparticles and enhancing them with a gold shell, we show potential for optical isolation, which is essential for a wide range of optical applications.
